title: Transmission finance reaches a closed infrastructure commitment before customer savings and reliability are realized
source_unit: U.S. Department of Energy Energy Dominance Financing Program project page for the AEP Texas transmission loan; official project-level financing and forecast claims, not customer billing data
geography: Texas; AEP transmission portfolio and 1.1 million projected customer beneficiaries

observations.period: July 2026; loan closing and project forecast

loan_amount.unit: US dollars, loan amount up to

transmission_scope.unit: miles of transmission lines to rebuild, reconductor, or build

capacity_forecast.unit: percent increase in power carrying capacity of existing infrastructure

projected_customer_savings.unit: US dollars of electricity cost savings over 30 years, projected for 1.1 million customers

projected_jobs.unit: permanent U.S. jobs supported, estimated at closing

realized_customer_outcome.unit: completed construction, interruption reduction, retail bill change, customer distribution, reliability, or durability

observations.method: DOE project-page extraction; closed financing, physical scope, capacity and customer-savings forecasts are kept separate from construction, operation, allocation, and household outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: The project page reports forecasts and a portfolio scope, not completed line miles, actual capacity, observed interruptions, customer bills, cost allocation, or realized savings. The 1.1 million customer figure is a forecast universe, not a linked household denominator.
observations.subgroup: Texas electricity customers, data-center and oil-and-gas loads, AEP Texas, workers, and communities along the transmission portfolio; incidence and benefit distribution are not reported.
observations.counterinterpretation: A closed loan can lower financing barriers and make construction more likely, while the investment may still produce real system value before individual bill savings can be assigned; forecast benefit is not proof of equal customer benefit.

boundary: This record adds a closed infrastructure-financing stage to the transmission and large-load route. It does not establish construction completion, operational reliability, customer bill savings, cost allocation, local burden, or geopolitical leverage. The next test requires project milestones, rate-case or bill data, outage/reliability measures, customer incidence, and durable operation kept separate.
